abstraction_design.rationale: Abstractions track the app's real variation well (render-prop extension, generic card builder, declarative columns) and the Moves pattern is thin enough that an Items clone costs little; CardData's accumulating optional fields are mild but keep it from being a showpiece.

findings.issue: The server/client boundary is convention-only: files in src/server/ are not covered by TanStack Start's default import protection, which matches **/*.server.* filenames or the @tanstack/react-start/server-only marker, so a careless client import of pokeapi.ts would bundle process.env/API code without a build error.
findings.suggestion: Rename the module (e.g. pokeapi.server.ts, functions split per resource) or add `import '@tanstack/react-start/server-only'` at the top of pokeapi.ts so the stable compiler enforces the boundary.

findings.issue: CardData is constructed in three independent places (toCards in pokeapi.ts:96, speciesIndex in pokeapi.ts:172, getTeamData here), so adding a card field or changing card semantics (e.g. sprite derivation) must be repeated and kept consistent.
findings.suggestion: Route getTeamData's member construction through toCards (or a shared cardOf(species) helper) so there is one card factory.

findings.issue: The generic card list embeds an ability-specific semantic (the 'hidden' flag and its note), so removing or restyling the abilities feature leaves dead logic in a component every page shares.
findings.suggestion: Generalize to a renderNote(card) prop (like the existing renderAction) or move the note to the abilities page via the existing extension point.

findings.issue: Sprite URLs are re-derived client-side by convention (mediaBase + /media/sprites/pokemon/<id>.png) instead of using the API-provided sprites.front_default, so a media-layout change is known in two layers (server apiBase + client spriteUrl).
findings.suggestion: Either keep the convention but document it in one place, or return a sprite URL with CardData from the server layer so the client never reconstructs API paths.

findings.issue: The page number is derived from whether the debounced query has caught up with the URL (`query === (search.q ?? '')`), making search and pagination edits easy to break silently.
findings.suggestion: Extract the query/page reconciliation into a small named hook (e.g. useDebouncedSearch) with a comment stating the invariant.

findings.issue: All page server functions live in one 230-line module, so every new resource section grows this file and it is the only merge-conflict hotspot in the codebase.
findings.suggestion: Split into server/functions/<resource>.ts files while the cost is still trivial; the uniform createServerFn pattern makes this a mechanical move.

findings.issue: MoveTable sort state is reset by an implicit key of `${p.game}-${table.method}`, so the reason tables remount on game change is not expressed anywhere.
findings.suggestion: Add a short comment (or a controlled sortKey prop on MoveTable) so future editors don't 'clean up' the key and reintroduce stale sort state.

summary: This is a well-layered, current-stable TanStack Start app: thin routes, one server data module with all API/cache knowledge, and shared components designed with render-prop seams rather than flags, so the common change scenarios land in one or two obvious places. The main editability costs are that CardData is assembled in three places, feature data layers live apart from their routes (making clean removal a three-layer grep), and the server/client boundary is convention rather than compiler-enforced. Nothing would block the pull request; the two medium findings are cheap follow-ups.
